claims.text: Lightweight HEAs can combine low density, mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance because of a single-phase solid-solution structure.
A single-phase solid solution enables a uniform distribution of constituent elements.
The single-phase structure maximizes configurational entropy.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid solution against phase separation and intermetallic formation.
Suppressing phase separation and intermetallic formation maintains mechanical strength.
Uniform elemental distribution enables formation of a uniform passive oxide layer.
Uniform elemental distribution reduces galvanic coupling.
Uniform elemental distribution reduces local elemental depletion.
Reduced galvanic coupling and local depletion improve corrosion and oxidation resistance.
Relative to a compositionally similar multiphase baseline, the single-phase HEA will have higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength.
Relative to the multiphase baseline, the single-phase HEA will have lower corrosion mass loss or current density.
Relative to the multiphase baseline, the single-phase HEA will have a lower high-temperature oxide-scale growth rate.
The single-phase HEA will have density comparable to or lower than that of the compositionally similar multiphase baseline.
The proposed benefits cease to hold when the composition contains elements with strong segregation tendencies.
The proposed benefits cease to hold when constituent elements are excessively volatile at the test temperature.
The proposed benefits cease to hold when processing induces phase separation, including through insufficient homogenization or rapid cooling.
A controlled comparison can be made between a single-phase lightweight HEA and a compositionally similar alloy engineered to contain multiple phases.
The comparison will measure strength, hardness, corrosion response, oxide-scale growth or mass gain, and density.
Oxidation resistance will be tested by thermogravimetric analysis at 800°C.
The hypothesis is falsified if the single-phase alloy fails to outperform the multiphase alloy in at least two of the three property categories while retaining comparable or lower density.
